texts.preamble: Sri. Santosh Kumar vs State Of Odisha on 9 February, 2026 Author: V. Narasingh Bench: V. Narasingh In The High Court Of Orissa At Cuttack Crl. Rev. No.781 of 2003 (In the matter of an application under Section 401 r/w Section 397 of Cr.P.C.) Sri. Santosh Kumar .... Petitioner Sahoo -versus- State of Odisha .... Opposite Party For Petitioner : Mr. P.K. Mishra, Advocate For Opposite Party : Mr. S. Panigrahi, Asc Coram: Justice V. Narasingh Date Of Hearing and Judgement: 09.02.2026 V. Narasingh,J.
texts.facts: The plea of the Petitioner was one of denial and false implication. To fortify their submission, the prosecution examined two witnesses P.W.1- the Food Inspector and P.W.2- Peon of C.D.M.O Office and several documents were exhibited and marked as. Ext. 1 to 9. Though one witness was examined on behalf of the Petitioner- accused D.W.1 , no documentary proof was exhibited.
texts.arguments: 6. Learned counsel Mr. Mishra, submits that both the learned Trial Court as well as the learned Appellate Court failed to take note of the statutory prescription contained in Section 10(7) and Section 13(2B) of the Act, 1954. For convenience of reference the said provisions are extracted hereunder: "xxx xxx xxx 10. Powers of Food Inspectors.-- (1) and (2) xxx xxx xxx (3) Where any sample is taken under clause (a) of sub- section (1) or sub-section (2), its cost calculated at the rate at which the article is usually sold to the public shall be paid to the person from whom it is taken. ( 4) to (6). xxx xxx xxx (7) Where the food inspector takes any action under clause (a) of sub-section (1), sub-section (2), sub-section (4), or sub-section (6), he shall, [call one or more persons to be present at the time when such action is taken and take his or their signatures]. xxx xxx xxx 13. Report of Public Analyst.-- (1) to (2A) xxx xxx xxx (2B) On receipt of the part or parts of the sample from the Local (Health) Authority under sub-section (2A) , the court shall first ascertain that the mark and seal or fastening as provided in clause (b) of sub-section (1) of section 11 are intact and the signature or thumb impression, as the case may be, is not tampered with, and dispatch the part or, as the case may be, one of the parts of the sample under its own seal to the Director of the Central Food Laboratory who shall thereupon send a certificate to the court in the prescribed form within one month from the date of receipt of the part of the sample specifying the result of the analysis. 7. It is submitted by the learned counsel for the Petitioner, Mr. Mishra, referring to the judgment of the Appellate Court, that though the attention of the learned Appellate Court was specifically drawn Sri. Santosh Kumar vs State Of Odisha on 9 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/106294141/ 2 to the infraction of Section 10(7) of the Act, 1954, the same was glossed over only referring to the evidence of P.W.1- the Food Inspector. So far as the 13(2B) of the Act, 1954 is concerned , there is no finding as such. 8. Per contra, learned public prosecutor submits that in the case at hand there is substantial compliance of Section 10(7) of the Act, 1954, since it is borne out from the record that the Food Inspector requested the persons present to act as witnesses but they declined. So far as 13(2B) of the Act, 1954 is concerned, it is dependent upon the steps taken pursuant to Section 13(2) of the Act, 1954 and there is nothing on record to indicate that any objection was raised to the sample received under Section 13(2) of the Act, 1954. 11. The finding of the learned Trial Court in this regard as referred to in paragraph-7 of the Appellate Court's order, wherein, while adverting to the alleged infraction of Section 10(7) of the Act, 1954, the learned Appellate Court allowed its judgment to be clouded by mechanically relying only on the evidence of P.W.1. The Court below convicted Sri. Santosh Kumar vs State Of Odisha on 9 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/106294141/ 3 and sentenced the appellant on the ground that he was selling adulterated food article i.e. chilli powder.
